name: emma
comment: The Prism's reader of what its person says to it (app/src/PrismEmma.lex.tex), held to W3C EMMA 1.0. Every prompt or gesture is one EMMA document; the request 'check' and a line end, then a document, answers 'malformed' when it is not well-formed namespace-aware XML, else 'conforms' or 'violates' with the Implementation Report Plan assertions it breaks, then ';' and the assertions whose features it shows. 'sources' pins the Recommendation, its schema and the Implementation Report Plan (the Working Group's inventory of testable assertions, ST-01's requirements for w3c-emma-1.0). The plan publishes no test documents, so the acceptance vectors are the Recommendation's own: 'documents' lists every <pre> block of the Recommendation that opens an emma:emma element, by its ordinal among all <pre> blocks, with markup removed and entities read, pinned by SHA-256; 'examples' carries those exact bytes. PrismPM compiles a guest's vectors within a fixed time, so they are held in two sets over the one guest: sections 2 to 4.1 here, sections 4.2 to Appendix C in app/specs/emma-annotations/spec.json. Four documents are not well-formed as W3C publishes them (14, 27, 65, 77), two elide lattice arcs with '...' and so break 603, 604 and 609 as written (17, 18), and one elides the interpretation (1, assertion 910). Each answer was also reached by a conforming XML parser reading the same bytes, outside the guest. The reader takes XML 1.0 without a DTD: elements, attributes, comments, CDATA and processing instructions, namespace declarations in scope, unique attributes; entity references are carried as written.
